procedure.description: periprosthetic capsulectomy, breast, with implant removal

denial.text: Northwind Mutual Health denied the claim for CPT 19371 (periprosthetic capsulectomy, breast, with implant removal) with date of service 2026-09-14. CARC 96: Non-covered charge(s). RARC N130: Consult plan benefit documents/guidelines for information about restrictions for this service. Payer remark: Revision of breast implants is considered cosmetic.

criteria.text: Baker grade III or IV capsular contracture with pain or deformity, or implant rupture confirmed by imaging.
The indication for the original implant placement is documented.
Symptoms documented for at least 3 months.

chart.text: Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.
From the referring physician: please evaluate for surgical management. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 2.0, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 100. Repeat in a year.

54 year old woman here about her implants. Discussed capsulectomy with implant removal and the options for replacement versus leaving them out. Her history otherwise: reflux on omeprazole as needed, anxiety, sees a counselor. Allergies: sulfa, hives as a child. Quit smoking 8 years ago, no alcohol, works two jobs. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Right breast is hard as a rock, distorted upward, tender to the touch, I would grade it Baker IV. Left is a Baker III, firm but not painful. Implants were placed in 2015 as part of her reconstruction after a right mastectomy for cancer, left side for symmetry. The hardening on the right started about 14 months ago and has gotten steadily worse, now hurts to lie on that side.
Work note requested for a sick day last Tuesday. Faxed to the employer.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.
MRI breast implants: right implant with a linguine sign consistent with intracapsular rupture, thickened capsule. Left implant intact with a thickened capsule and no rupture.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, she will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.

Called her with the cholesterol results. Total 184, LDL 137, HDL 59, triglycerides 187. Discussed diet and walking. She wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
Back to go over the MRI and the plan. She wants the right one out and both capsules addressed. Vitals today 137 over 69, pulse 67.
Patient called about a tick bite on the calf after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.
Message from the patient about scheduling. Wants a date in the next couple of months if the insurance comes through. Passed to the surgery scheduler.

Mole on the left forearm that her spouse noticed. About 7 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.
She called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in the fall. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.
A1c came back 6.0. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. She is motivated.

Here with a cough and congestion for 8 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if she gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 5 years.

Twisted the left ankle stepping off a curb 3 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the right for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 15 and 18. No ocular pathology noted.
Check-in while we wait on the insurance. No change in the complaints. Reviewed the risks and recovery one more time, she remains sure about going ahead.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.
Blood pressure check. 127 over 77 today, 132 over 85 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 10 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 6 weeks.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 40. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.

Knee pain going down stairs, left side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.
Pre-op. Consent signed for bilateral capsulectomy with implant removal, right side en bloc if the capsule allows. Labs fine.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 96 denial can be answered from the record.
